slides.headline: Claude is getting a new home: Anthropic just locked in a *20-year data center* in Canada

image.generate: Vertical photo at dusk on a rugged rocky coastline in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia. A long, low, windowless modern data center building with a dark gray metal facade sits on the cliff in the right two thirds of the frame, with a single warm orange light, the same orange as the shape in the first image, glowing from an open loading door. Behind it, tall white wind turbines stand on green hills under a dramatic stormy sky, with plenty of headroom above the turbines. Cold Atlantic waves crash on the rocks below. The left third of the frame is empty dark sky and sea. The bottom third is dark rocks and water. Blank surfaces, no readable text or labels on any object, no letters, no logos, no watermarks. Photorealistic, high contrast, one clear subject. It must look like an unedited real photo from a news agency, not a painting, not digital art, no glow effects.

slides.heading: Anthropic's *first in Canada*
paras: Anthropic has signed a 20-year lease for an 18,600 square meter data center in Point Tupper, Cape Breton, to power its Claude AI assistant.
Reuters called it the Claude maker's first data center agreement in Canada. Developer EverWind Fuels did not disclose what the lease is worth.

slides.heading: A *C$10 billion* bet
paras: EverWind says the full plan is worth C$10 billion, the largest private investment in Nova Scotia's history: C$8 billion for the campus and C$2 billion for wind farms.
Phase one draws 95 megawatts and is due online in late 2027. A 325 megawatt expansion in mid-2028 would bring total demand to 420 megawatts.

slides.heading: Jobs, wind and *water*
paras: The project promises 2,000 construction jobs and 215 permanent positions. EverWind says it will pay for grid upgrades so local ratepayers are not charged.

paras.t: Cooling water comes from nearby Landrie Lake in a closed loop. Opposition NDP leader Claudia Chender says the premier is asking people to just trust his word.

slides.hook: The race for AI power just reached Cape Breton. Follow to see where Claude grows next.
